To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of the optimal selection strategies is very good, that the performance of suboptimal selection strategies is also very good in most cases, and that with minimal CSI almost the same performance can be achieved as with perfect CSI.
for regenerative relays with limited channel knowledge the selection of the best relay is not necessarily the optimal selection strategy.
in dual-hop systems with regenerative relay nodes it is possible to achieve almost the same performance with minimal CSI as with perfect CSI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the selection of the best relay for a dual-hop transmission.
the problem of relay selection in dual-hop transmission systems.
the selection of the best relay for dual-hop communication systems, where the relay tries to fully decode the received message.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selection strategies presented in this paper should always be used in practice.
the selection strategy is of utmost importance for the performance and that it can even outperform the performance of the best relay in a network.
the selection strategy with minimal CSI is a reasonable choice for practical systems, since it is not only simple but also provides almost the same performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
with only a little additional overhead the performance can be improved by a large factor.
the selection strategy is not the key issue in the dual-hop communication systems, but the channel conditions are the main factors.
the selection strategy for dual-hop systems is not as important as for single-hop systems and the main focus should be put on the design of efficient relays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
with a proper selection strategy, dual-hop communication systems are very well suited for applications in which a high reliability and/or a good performance is required.
with only very limited CSI at the selecting entity, almost optimal relay selection can be performed.
in most practical scenarios it is not necessary to have perfect CSI to obtain near-optimal results.
